content_units: Cape Town Home Office Plan Snapshot

For a two-person home office with daily video calls, cloud backups, and occasional 4K streaming,   fiber uncapped   is the safest fit. Under your   ZAR 900/month   limit, the strongest overall choice is   Plan B   if you want the least friction, while   Plan A   is the best value pick.
Context used:
- Two concurrent work users
- Frequent video calls
- Ongoing cloud sync/backups
- Occasional 4K streaming
- Cape Town fixed-line fiber is generally more stable than LTE for home-office use
Internet Plan Comparison
Plan   Type   Speed   Monthly Price   Reliability   Best Fit   Value View
Plan A   Fiber uncapped   50/25 Mbps     ZAR 699     High   Strong home office + backups + 4K     Best value
Plan B   Fiber uncapped   100/50 Mbps     ZAR 899     High   Heavy cloud use + smoother multitasking     Best overall
Plan C   LTE capped   80 GB peak + 80 GB off-peak     ZAR 599     Medium   Light/moderate users, backup line   Weak for your usage
Plan D   Fiber uncapped   25/10 Mbps     ZAR 549     High   Basic remote work, lighter uploads   Budget option
Speed, Reliability, and Value Trade-offs
Plan B fiber 100/50 Mbps — best overall under budget
-   Speed:   Easily handles two HD video calls, cloud backups in the background, and 4K streaming with the most headroom.
-   Reliability:   Fiber is usually the most stable option for latency-sensitive work like Zoom, Teams, and VPN use.
-   Value trade-off:   It costs the most, but still fits your cap by   ZAR 1  . You’re paying for smoother peak-time performance and faster uploads.
Plan A fiber 50/25 Mbps — best value recommendation
-   Speed:   Very solid for two people working from home, including concurrent video calls and routine cloud sync.
-   Reliability:   Same key fiber advantage as Plan B: more consistent performance than LTE.
-   Value trade-off:   At   ZAR 200 less than Plan B  , this is the sweet spot if you want strong performance without paying for extra headroom you may not always use.
Plan D fiber 25/10 Mbps — workable but tighter
-   Speed:   Fine for browsing, office apps, and one or two calls, but it gets tighter when uploads, backups, and streaming overlap.
-   Reliability:   Still better than LTE because it is uncapped fiber.
-   Value trade-off:   Cheap and usable, but the   10 Mbps upload   is the main constraint for cloud backups and simultaneous calls.
Plan C LTE 80 + 80 GB — lowest fit for your needs
-   Speed:   LTE speeds can look good on paper, but performance varies by signal strength, tower load, and time of day.
-   Reliability:   Less predictable than fiber for work calls and large backups; latency and congestion can be noticeable.
-   Value trade-off:   Cheapest non-fiber alternative, but the   data cap   is the real problem. Two home-office users plus cloud backup and 4K can burn through this quickly.
Recommended Pick for Your Setup
Recommended: Plan A fiber 50/25 Mbps at ZAR 699
Why this is the best fit:
- Enough speed for   two simultaneous work-from-home users
-   25 Mbps upload   is much better than Plan D for cloud backups and call quality
-   Uncapped   means no stress about backup jobs or streaming usage
- Costs materially less than Plan B while still covering your stated needs well
Upgrade to Plan B   if:
- You upload large files often
- You want backups to finish faster with less impact on work
- You expect more than occasional 4K streaming
- You prefer extra performance cushion for the next 1–2 years
Skip Plan C   unless:
- Fiber is unavailable at your address
- It is only a temporary or backup connection
